title: The Search for the Wicked Witch, part 10
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The little girl, seeing she had lost one of her pretty shoes, grew angry, and said to the Witch, “Give me back my shoe!”
“I will not,” retorted the Witch, “for it is now my shoe, and not yours.”
“You are a wicked creature!” cried Dorothy. “You have no right to take my shoe from me.”
“I shall keep it, just the same,” said the Witch, laughing at her, “and someday I shall get the other one from you, too.”
This made Dorothy so very angry that she picked up the bucket of water that stood near and dashed it over the Witch, wetting her from head to foot.
Instantly the wicked woman gave a loud cry of fear, and then, as Dorothy looked at her in wonder, the Witch began to shrink and fall away.
“See what you have done!” she screamed. “In a minute I shall melt away.”
“I’m very sorry, indeed,” said Dorothy, who was truly frightened to see the Witch actually melting away like brown sugar before her very eyes.
“Didn’t you know water would be the end of me?” asked the Witch, in a wailing, despairing voice.
“Of course not,” answered Dorothy. “How should I?”

“Well, in a few minutes I shall be all melted, and you will have the castle to yourself. I have been wicked in my day, but I never thought a little girl like you would ever be able to melt me and end my wicked deeds. Look out—here I go!”

With these words the Witch fell down in a brown, melted, shapeless mass and began to spread over the clean boards of the kitchen floor. Seeing that she had really melted away to nothing, Dorothy drew another bucket of water and threw it over the mess. She then swept it all out the door. After picking out the silver shoe, which was all that was left of the old woman, she cleaned and dried it with a cloth, and put it on her foot again. Then, being at last free to do as she chose, she ran out to the courtyard to tell the Lion that the Wicked Witch of the West had come to an end, and that they were no longer prisoners in a strange land.

options: That she give back the shoe
That she free the Lion
That she send her to Kansas
That she leave Toto alone

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Dorothy pick up and throw?
options: The bucket of water standing near
The bar of iron from the floor
The Witch's own umbrella
A pot from the kitchen shelf

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Witch say would happen in a minute?
options: That she would melt away
That she would call the Monkeys
That she would take the other shoe
That she would freeze solid

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Witch melt into?
options: A brown, melted, shapeless mass
A puddle of clear water
A heap of fine black coal
A cloud of gray smoke

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was left of the old woman?
options: The silver shoe
The Golden Cap
Her umbrella
Nothing whatever

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did Dorothy throw the water?
options: She was made very angry by the Witch's mockery
She had guessed that water would destroy her
The Lion had shouted to her to do it
She was trying to wash the floor clean

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Dorothy know about water and the Witch?
options: Nothing at all, as she told the Witch herself
That it was the Witch's one weakness
That the Good Witch had warned her of it
That the Winkies had told her the secret

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Dorothy feel as the Witch melted?
options: Truly frightened, and sorry for what she had done
Delighted at her own sudden victory over her
Indifferent to whatever became of the Witch
Afraid the Winkies would blame her for it

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does despairing describe about the Witch's voice?
options: Without any hope left
Loud enough to fill the castle
Sweet and pleading
Sharp with anger

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: An angry accident ends the Witch and frees her prisoners
A careful plan of Dorothy's destroys the Witch at last
The Witch takes both shoes and Dorothy gives up hope
The Lion breaks out of the yard and kills the Witch

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Witch say she would do someday?
options: Get the other shoe from Dorothy too
Melt Dorothy as she had the others
Call the Winged Monkeys once more
Set the Lion free to hunt

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Dorothy do with the melted mess?
options: Threw more water on it and swept it out the door
Left it where it lay and ran outside
Covered it over with the Witch's cloak
Called the Winkies in to clear it away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy do with the recovered shoe?
options: Cleaned and dried it and put it on again
Threw it out of the door with the mess
Gave it to the Lion to keep safe
Left it lying on the kitchen floor

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Witch admit at the end?
options: That she never thought a little girl could end her
That she had been good once, long ago

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, where did Dorothy run when it was over?
options: To the courtyard, to tell the Lion
To the kitchen, to finish her work
Out of the castle and towards the East
To the cupboard, to find the Golden Cap

options: Answered back sharply

Whispered in reply
Refused to answer

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?

A long battle in which Dorothy defeats a powerful witch
